chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who hired an animal, so he gave it to someone else, and it died. He said: If he had stipulated that no one else would ride it, he is responsible for it, and if he did not specify, there is nothing upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on liability if a hired animal dies while used by someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of conditional liability in Islamic contract law, distinguishing between explicit stipulations (shart) and general usage rights. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the specificity of contractual terms in determining risk allocation, a concept rooted in the Prophetic tradition of 'gharar' (uncertainty) avoidance. The ruling underscores that liability is not automatic but contingent upon the agreed-upon scope of permission granted to the sub-user.
